## Evaluation
I will evaluate the build with pass^k: run the agent k times on the same task and count it as a success only if all k runs succeed. This is a reliability-focused metric, which matches deployment better than pass@k.

I will also use a direct measure rather than only a proxy. For example, if I want to know whether the system is actually robust, I will look at repeated-task success / retention over time rather than relying only on a single quiz or demo performance.

args.text:
Yes — pass^k means “all k attempts pass.”

So if k = 3, you run the same build 3 separate times:
- run 1: success
- run 2: success
- run 3: success

That counts as pass^3.
If even one run fails, then it is not pass^3.

Why use it? Because it measures reliability, not just whether the system can succeed once. For a Friday build, that’s usually the safer metric.

Quick check: if a system succeeds on 4 out of 5 runs, is that pass@5 or pass^5?
